mainTopic: An אלמנה's twenty-five-year limit on her כתובה, the case of רב חייא אריכא, and the start of the משנה of אדמון and חנן
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of an אלמנה who waits about twenty-five years without claiming her כתובה. If she holds the actual שטר כתובה, everyone agrees she can collect forever. The מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and the חכמים applies only when she has no שטר, and the הלכה follows the חכמים. Next, בר קפרא and רב say the twenty-five years cost her only the basic מנה or מאתים, so she keeps the תוספת. רבי יוחנן says she loses the תוספת too, because a תנאי כתובה is like the כתובה itself. The גמרא then tells the story of רב חייא אריכא, who supported his widowed sister-in-law in her father's house for twenty-five years. רבה בר שילא ruled that she kept her כתובה, because embarrassment had kept her from asking, and רבא agreed. But רבא denied her claim to the produce of the land, because her אדרכתא failed to say which fields had belonged to her late husband. That was a real mistake, not a טעות סופר. The פרק הנושא then ends, and a new chapter opens with the משנה of the two judges אדמון and חנן בן אבישלום.

steps.title: The count restarts, and a written כתובה is collectible forever
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier teaching. In the case it was discussing, the twenty-five years start over. And if she holds her שטר כתובה, she can collect at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is as she was at the beginning. And if a marriage document is in her hands, she collects her כתובה forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that began just before this. It says the twenty-five-year clock starts over in that case, and that holding the שטר כתובה lets her collect forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea behind the twenty-five-year limit is that an אלמנה who waits that long without asking for her כתובה is assumed to have given it up. Holding the written שטר is strong evidence that she never gave it up, so the time limit does not apply. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: As at the beginning: the twenty-five-year count starts over
The written marriage contract document
Literally 'comes out from under her hand': she has it and can show it
Collects payment
Forever, with no time limit

steps.whyThisMatters: This line about the written שטר is exactly what the next question is built on.

phrases.english: She is as at the beginning.
phrases.notes: This finishes a case from just before here. The twenty-five years start counting again from zero.

phrases.english: And if a marriage contract document
is in her possession,
she collects her marriage contract forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The count restarts. A woman holding her שטר כתובה can collect forever, with no twenty-five-year limit.

steps.title: Where does the dispute apply, and who is the הלכה like?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sends a two-part question to רב נחמן בר יעקב. First, does the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and the חכמים apply when she holds the שטר, or only when she does not? Second, which side does the הלכה follow?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sent to רב נחמן בר יעקב: Teach us, our teacher: is the dispute when the שטר כתובה is in her hands, or when it is not in her hands? And the הלכה follows whose words?
steps.whatsHappening: A student sends a letter to his teacher with two questions about the משנה's מחלוקת. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about when an אלמנה loses her כתובה after twenty-five years. The question is whether that argument covers even a woman who holds her שטר, or only a woman without one. He also wants a practical ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him, a written message to someone in another place
Our teacher, teach us: a respectful way to open a question
Dispute
And the practical law follows whose opinion?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda sent
to Rav Naḥman bar Ya'akov:
Let our teacher teach us,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁשְּׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדָהּ מַחְלוֹקֶת,
phrases.english: is the dispute when a marriage contract is in her possession,
phrases.notes: The dispute is the one in the משנה between רבי מאיר and the חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כְּשֶׁאֵין שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדָהּ?
phrases.english: or when a marriage contract is not in her possession?
And the halakha is in accordance with whose words?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the line about holding the שטר and asks how it fits the משנה's מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the מחלוקת covers a woman who holds her שטר כתובה, and which side the הלכה follows.

steps.title: The dispute is only without a שטר, and the הלכה follows the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יעקב answers that the מחלוקת applies only when she has no שטר. With a שטר, everyone agrees she collects forever. The הלכה follows the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back: When the שטר כתובה is not in her hands, there is a dispute. But if the שטר כתובה is in her hands, she collects her כתובה forever. And the הלכה follows the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The teacher answers both questions. The argument is only about a woman without the document, and in practice we follow the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding the שטר takes the case out of the מחלוקת completely, because everyone agrees she has not given up her rights. For a woman without the שטר, the time limit applies the way the חכמים describe it in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But: marks the case that is different
The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי מאיר

steps.whatToRemember: With a שטר כתובה in hand, an אלמנה collects forever according to everyone. Without one, there is a מחלוקת, and the הלכה follows the חכמים.

phrases.english: He sent to him:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשֶׁאֵין שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדָהּ מַחְלוֹקֶת,
phrases.english: When a marriage contract is not in her possession, there is a dispute,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדָהּ —
phrases.english: but when a marriage contract is in her possession,
she collects her marriage contract forever.
And the halakha is in accordance with the words of the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: בְּשֶׁאֵין שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדָהּ מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both parts of the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת is only when there is no שטר. With a שטר she collects forever according to everyone, and the הלכה follows the חכמים.

steps.title: The time limit covers only the basic כתובה, not the תוספת
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports a teaching of בר קפרא, passed down through רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי שמעון בן פזי. The twenty-five-year loss applies only to the basic מנה or מאתים. She still keeps the right to the תוספת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: רבי שמעון בן פזי said that רבי יהושע בן לוי said in the name of בר קפרא: They only taught this about the מנה or מאתים. But the תוספת, she still has.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching arrives from ארץ ישראל. It limits the twenty-five-year rule to the basic כתובה sum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic כתובה is a fixed sum set by the חכמים: מאתים for a בתולה, and מנה for a widow or divorcee. The תוספת is the extra amount the husband added on his own. Even after twenty-five years she is not assumed to have given up the תוספת. This opinion is part of a larger discussion that continues afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings
They taught this only about: a phrase that narrows a rule
One hundred or two hundred דינרים, the basic כתובה amounts
The extra sum the husband added to the basic כתובה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say the time limit has no effect. She still loses the basic מנה or מאתים. Only the תוספת stays hers.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came:
Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
in the name of bar Kappara:
They taught only about one hundred or two hundred,
phrases.notes: 'They taught' means the rule that she loses her כתובה after twenty-five years.

phrases.english: but the additional sum, she has.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new limit on the twenty-five-year rule: which part of the כתובה it covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The twenty-five-year loss applies only to the basic מנה or מאתים. The אלמנה keeps her right to the תוספת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says she loses the extra amount too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that after twenty-five years she loses even the תוספת. The reason comes from רבי ינאי: the extra terms of a כתובה count just like the כתובה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: She does not get even the extra amount. This is because רבי אייבו said in the name of רבי ינאי: The terms added to a כתובה are treated just like the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an opinion that argues against בר קפרא from the previous step. רבי יוחנן says the widow loses everything, including the תוספת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא split the כתובה into two parts: the basic sum, which is lost, and the תוספת, which is kept. רבי יוחנן refuses to split them. Because of רבי ינאי's rule that a תנאי כתובה is like the כתובה itself, giving up the basic sum also means giving up the extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra amount the husband added on top of the basic כתובה
A condition or term written into the כתובה
It is treated just like the כתובה itself

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
She does not have even the additional sum.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Aivu said that Rabbi Yannai said:
A stipulation in the marriage contract is like the marriage contract itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opinion that argues with בר קפרא's ruling in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After twenty-five years she loses even the תוספת, because a תנאי כתובה is treated like the כתובה.

steps.title: רב agrees she keeps the extra amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב also taught that only the basic מנה or מאתים is lost, while the תוספת stays.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא, who said in the name of רב: The rule was taught only about the basic hundred or two hundred. She still gets the extra amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement, from רב, that matches בר קפרא's view. The widow keeps her תוספת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אתמר נמי shows that בר קפרא's view in Step 4 was also taught by a different chain of אמוראים. This adds weight to the side that says she keeps the תוספת, against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (another source teaches the same thing)
They taught this only about
The basic כתובה: one hundred zuz (for a widow or divorcee) or two hundred zuz (for a בתולה)

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
They taught this only about the one hundred or two hundred,
but she does have the additional sum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to support בר קפרא's view, against רבי יוחנן in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the basic מנה or מאתים is lost after twenty-five years; she keeps the תוספת.

steps.title: רבי אבא asks whether רב really said this
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks רב הונא if רב really taught this. רב הונא answers with his own question: are you asking because you disagree, or because you like the ruling?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רב הונא: Did רב really say this? רב הונא answered: Are you saying this to quiet me, or to give me a drink?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא questions the report of רב's ruling. רב הונא wants to know what lies behind the question, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Did רב say this?" could show surprise and disagreement, or it could show delight. רב הונא asks which one he means. Either he wants to shut down the ruling, or he likes it so much he wants to reward the teacher with a drink.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רב really say this?
To silence me (from the root "to be quiet")
To give me a drink

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rav Huna:
Did Rav really say this?
He said to him:
Are you saying this to silence me,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the ן in round brackets. Either way the word means "to silence."

phrases.english: or are you saying this to give me a drink?
phrases.notes: Meaning: are you so pleased with this ruling that you want to treat me to some wine?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב הוּנָא: אֲמַר רַב הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reported ruling of רב in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אבא's question shows disagreement with רב's ruling or approval of it.

steps.title: רבי אבא admits he disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that he asked in order to silence רב הונא. This means he disagrees with רב and sides with רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am saying it to silence you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers that his question was meant to challenge the ruling, not to praise it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer shows that רבי אבא does not accept the ruling that she keeps the תוספת. He leans toward רבי יוחנן, who says she loses everything. So the מחלוקת from Steps 4 to 6 stays open, with strong voices on each side.

keyTerms.meaning: I am saying

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. בר קפרא and רב say that after twenty-five years only the basic מנה or מאתים is lost and she keeps the תוספת. רבי יוחנן (and רבי אבא) say that because a תנאי כתובה is like the כתובה, she loses the תוספת as well.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am saying it to silence you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's question from Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אבא asked in order to silence, meaning he disagrees with רב's ruling that she keeps the תוספת.

steps.title: The story of רב חייא אריכא and his mother-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story. רב חייא אריכא's mother-in-law was also his brother's widow, and he supported her for twenty-five years while she lived in her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The mother-in-law of רב חייא אריכא was also his brother's wife. She was a widow living in her father's house, and he supported her for twenty-five years in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story connected to the twenty-five-year rule. It lays out the facts here, setting up a question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts match our topic closely: a widow, living in her father's house, and twenty-five years. That raises the question of whether she has lost her כתובה, even though she was being supported the whole time. The גמרא is setting up that discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother-in-law
His brother's wife
And he supported her (gave her food and upkeep)
In her father's house

phrases.english: The mother-in-law of Rav Ḥiyya Arikha
was his brother's wife,
and she was a widow living in her father's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְזָנַהּ עֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמֵשׁ שְׁנִין בְּבֵי נָשָׁא.
phrases.english: and he supported her for twenty-five years in her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמָתֵיהּ דְּרַב חִיָּיא אֲרִיכָא אִינְתַּת אֲחוּהּ הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the תוספת debate to a real-life case about a widow, her father's house, and twenty-five years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: a widow living in her father's house was supported by רב חייא אריכא for twenty-five years.

steps.title: She demands support and her כתובה, and he refuses both
steps.stepSummary: After twenty-five years, the widow asks רב חייא אריכא for food support and then for her כתובה. He tells her she is owed neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end she said to him: 'Give me my food support.' He said: 'You are not owed food support.' She said: 'Then give me my כתובה.' He said: 'You are owed neither food support nor a כתובה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The widow makes her demands, and רב חייא אריכא refuses both of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is relying on the rule that a widow living in her father's house loses her כתובה after twenty-five years. Since the כתובה is gone, he says her food support is gone too. This sets up the court case that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Food support. A widow is owed this from her husband's estate.
The marriage contract payment owed to a woman when her marriage ends.
You don't have (any claim).

phrases.english: At the end she said to him:
Give me food support.
He said to her: You are not owed food support.
Give me my marriage contract payment.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: לָא מְזוֹנֵי אִית לִיךְ,
phrases.english: He said to her: You are not owed food support,
and you are not owed a marriage contract payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The heir claims that after twenty-five years in her father's house, the widow has lost both her food support and her כתובה.

steps.title: She takes him to court, and the judge asks for the facts
steps.stepSummary: The widow brings רב חייא אריכא before רבה בר שילא, who asks him to describe exactly what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: She summoned him to court before רבה בר שילא. The judge said to him: 'Tell me, then, what exactly happened in this case?'
steps.whatsHappening: The case goes to court. רבה בר שילא asks for the exact facts, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge does not rule right away. He wants the details first, because the details of how she was supported will decide the case.

keyTerms.meaning: She summoned him to court.
The actual facts of the case.
The judge who heard the case.

phrases.english: She summoned him to judgment
before Rabba bar Sheila.
He said to him: Tell me, then,
what exactly happened in the case?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא לִי אִיזִי גּוּפָא דְעוֹבָדָא הֵיכִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The dispute from Step 10 is brought to a judge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact facts of how the widow was supported.

steps.title: He supported her personally for twenty-five years
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא אריכא says he supported her for twenty-five years in her father's house and personally carried her food to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'I supported her for twenty-five years in her father's house. I swear by your life, I carried it to her on my own shoulders.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא אריכא answers the judge. He stresses that she lived in her father's house the whole time and that he supported her faithfully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He means this as proof that she was cared for in her father's house for twenty-five years, so the rule that she loses her כתובה should apply. But the detail that he carried her food himself will end up working against him in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: I supported her.
In her family's house, meaning her father's house.
By your life, Master. An expression like an oath.

phrases.english: He said to him: I supported her
for twenty-five years in her father's house,
by the life of the Master,
I carried it to her on my own shoulders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זָנִיתַהּ עֶשְׂרִים וַחֲמֵשׁ שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the judge's question from Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She lived in her father's house for twenty-five years, and he personally brought her support the whole time.

steps.title: The ruling: she was too embarrassed to ask, so she collects
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא rules that she keeps her כתובה. He uses the same reason that protects a widow in her husband's house: she held back from asking out of embarrassment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Why did the חכמים say that as long as she lives in her husband's house she can collect her כתובה forever? Because we say she did not demand it out of embarrassment. Here too, she did not demand it out of embarrassment. Go pay her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The judge gives his ruling. He takes the reason behind the rule for a widow in her husband's house and applies it to this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of losing the כתובה after twenty-five years is based on the idea that her silence means she gave it up. A widow in her husband's house is an exception, because her silence comes from embarrassment, not from giving up. Since the heir treated this widow with such personal respect, she was embarrassed in the same way, so her silence does not count as giving up.

keyTerms.meaning: Embarrassment.
In her husband's house.
She can collect her כתובה at any time, with no time limit.
Go give it to her.

steps.whatToRemember: The real issue is not where she lives. It is why she stayed silent. If her silence came from embarrassment, she has not given up her כתובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a rule's reason can stretch it to a new case. The reason behind 'her husband's house' also covers a widow in her father's house who was treated with great respect.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טַעְמָא מַאי אֲמוּר רַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: He said to him: What is the reason the Rabbis said:
as long as she is in her husband's house
she collects her marriage contract payment forever?
phrases.notes: This is the rule from our משנה for a widow living in her husband's house.

phrases.english: Because we say: it is due to embarrassment
that she did not demand it.
Here too: it is due to embarrassment
that she did not demand it.
Go give it to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the facts from Step 12 to give a ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow who did not demand her כתובה out of embarrassment does not lose it after twenty-five years, even if she lives in her father's house.

steps.title: He ignores the ruling, and the court lets her seize his property
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא אריכא ignores the ruling. רבה בר שילא then writes the widow an authorization to collect from his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He paid no attention. So the judge wrote her an authorization to collect from his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. The heir refuses to pay, and the court enforces its ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אדרכתא is a court document that lets the creditor take the debtor's property. It shows that רבה בר שילא stood firmly behind his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He paid no attention; he ignored it.
A court authorization to seize a debtor's property.
Property.

steps.confusionAlert: The 'he' changes here. רב חייא אריכא is the one who ignored the ruling, but רבה בר שילא, the judge, is the one who wrote the authorization.

phrases.english: He paid no attention.
He wrote her an authorization to collect from his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened after the ruling in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court enforces the widow's right by giving her an authorization to collect from the heir's property.

steps.title: רבא approves the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא אריכא complains to רבא about how he was judged. רבא answers that he was judged correctly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבא and said: 'Look, Master, how he judged me!' רבא said to him: 'He judged you well.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא אריכא appeals, and a higher authority, רבא, confirms that רבה בר שילא's ruling was right. The story continues in the next step, when the widow asks רבא for the produce of the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's approval makes the embarrassment reasoning the accepted conclusion of the story. A widow treated with great respect by the heir keeps her כתובה even after twenty-five years in her father's house.

keyTerms.meaning: Look, Master. A respectful way to ask someone to consider something.
He judged you well.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא confirms the ruling: when the heir's honorable treatment made her too embarrassed to ask, she keeps her כתובה even after twenty-five years.

phrases.english: He came before Rava,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי מָר הֵיכִי דָּנַן!
phrases.english: He said to him: Let the Master see how he judged me!
He said to him: He judged you well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The heir appeals the ruling from Steps 13-14, and the ruling is upheld.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא upholds רבה בר שילא: silence that comes from embarrassment does not cancel a widow's כתובה, even after twenty-five years in her father's house.

steps.title: The widow demands the produce since her authorization
steps.stepSummary: Building on רבא's approval of the ruling, the widow demands all the produce of the land from the day of the authorization until now.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: If so, let him go and give me back the produce from that day until now.
steps.whatsHappening: The widow speaks to רבא. Since the ruling in her favor was correct, she now asks for the produce the land grew from the day she was authorized to collect it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her logic is that once the court authorized her to take the land, it was hers from that day. So everything it produced since then should also be hers. This opens a new question about פירות, not just about the land itself.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if that is true
Produce or fruits: what the land yields
Now, today

phrases.english: She said to him: If so,
phrases.notes: "She" is the widow, and "him" is רבא, who just said the ruling against רב חייא אריכא was correct.

phrases.english: let him go and return to me the produce
from that day until now.
phrases.notes: "That day" means the day her authorization to collect from his property was written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's confirmation of the ruling to make a further claim for produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The widow claims the land's produce from the date of the authorization.

steps.title: רבא finds a missing line in the authorization
steps.stepSummary: רבא examines the אדרכתא and finds that it lacks a line stating the land belonged to the deceased. He rules that it was not written properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Show me your authorization. He saw that it did not say: "And it is known to us that these properties belong to the deceased." He said to her: The authorization is not written properly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks to see her document. He notices an important line is missing and tells her the document is flawed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An authorization should state that the land taken came from the dead husband's estate, since only his property is tied to the כתובה. Without that line, the document is defective. So the land does not count as hers from the day it was written, and she loses her claim to the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: A court document authorizing a creditor to search out and seize the debtor's property
It is known to us: a clause in which the court confirms a fact
The deceased
Not written properly

phrases.english: He said to her: Show me your authorization.
He saw that it was not written in it:
"And it is known to us that these properties
are those of the deceased."
phrases.notes: The "deceased" is her husband, רב חייא אריכא's brother.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: אַדְרָכְתָּא לָאו שַׁפִּיר כְּתִיבָא.
phrases.english: He said to her: The authorization is not written properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the widow's produce claim by finding a flaw in her document.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Her claim to produce from the date of the authorization
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The authorization lacks the clause stating the land belonged to the deceased.

steps.title: She asks for produce from the end of the announcement period
steps.stepSummary: The widow gives up on the authorization date and asks for produce from the day the court's announcement period ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Forget the authorization. Let me take the produce from the day the announcement days were completed until now.
steps.whatsHappening: The widow makes a smaller claim. Even if the document is flawed, she wants at least the produce from a later date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before giving land to a creditor, the court announces it publicly for a set period. She argues that once that period ended, the land should count as hers, whatever is wrong with the document. So she should get the produce from then on.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it go: forget about it
Days of announcement: the period when the court publicly announces land for sale or collection
I will take

phrases.english: She said to him: Let the authorization go,
let me take [the produce] from the day
that the days of announcement were completed, until now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against step 17 with a fallback claim.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if the document is flawed, the completed announcement period should make the land hers from then on.

steps.title: A document with an error gives no rights at all
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the end of the announcement period counts only when the authorization has no error. A flawed authorization gives her nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: That applies only where no error is written in the authorization. But where an error is written in it, we have nothing to do with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects her fallback claim. The announcement-period rule works only with a properly written authorization.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her whole collection process rests on the authorization. If the document itself contains a mistake, the process built on it, including the announcement period, does not give her rights to the produce. So she gets no produce at all.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply: this rule holds only in a certain case
An error
We have nothing to do with it: it has no force

phrases.english: He said to her: This applies
where no error is written in the authorization,
but where an error is written in the authorization,
we have nothing to do with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא כְּתִיב טָעוּתָא בְּאַדְרָכְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by limiting the announcement-period rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to a case without a written error
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The end of the announcement period always gives the creditor rights to the produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: It does so only when the authorization is free of errors.

steps.title: She cites רבא's own rule about scribal error
steps.stepSummary: The widow challenges רבא with his own ruling that a missing אחריות clause is treated as a טעות סופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: But aren't you, Master, the one who said that a missing guarantee clause is a scribal error?
steps.whatsHappening: The widow uses רבא's own teaching against him. If a missing guarantee clause counts as a copying slip, the missing line here should too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that when a sale document leaves out the guarantee clause, we assume the scribe forgot it and treat it as written. She argues the same should apply here: read the missing line into her authorization and make it valid.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it you, Master, who said: quoting someone's own ruling back to him
A guarantee clause: the seller's commitment to pay back the buyer if the land is taken away
A scribe's error: an accidental omission by the writer

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: וְהָא מָר הוּא דְּאָמַר
phrases.english: She said to him: But isn't it you, Master, who said
[a missing] guarantee is a scribal error?
phrases.notes: She means that if a document leaves out the guarantee, we treat it as if the scribe simply forgot to write it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מָר הוּא דְּאָמַר אַחְרָיוּת טָעוּת סוֹפֵר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in steps 17 and 19 using his own principle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the flawed authorization gives her nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a missing אחריות clause is read in as a טעות סופר, the missing clause here should be read in as well.

steps.title: This omission was a real mistake in judgment, not a slip
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that this case cannot be called a טעות סופר, because even רבה בר שילא made this mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to her: In this case one cannot say it is a scribal error, because here even רבה בר שילא made a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why his scribal-error rule does not help her. Here the line was left out on purpose, not by accident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טעות סופר means the writer meant to include something and forgot. Here רבה בר שילא, the judge himself, thought the line was not needed. So it was not a slip. It was a deliberate choice, and we cannot pretend it was written.

keyTerms.meaning: One cannot say
Erred, made a mistake

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of mistakes. A טעות סופר is an accidental slip of the pen, which we can fix by reading the words in. Here the judge left the line out on purpose because he got the law wrong, so it cannot be read in.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ רָבָא: בְּהָא לֵיכָּא לְמֵימַר
phrases.english: Rava said to her: In this case one cannot say
it is a scribal error,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא טָעֵי.
phrases.english: because in this even רבה בר שילא erred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ רָבָא: בְּהָא לֵיכָּא לְמֵימַר טָעוּת סוֹפֵר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by showing the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a deliberate omission versus an accidental one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any missing standard clause can be treated as a טעות סופר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an accidental omission counts. Here the judge left the line out on purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit of the טעות סופר principle: we fill in a missing clause only when we can assume the writer meant to include it.

steps.title: Why רבה בר שילא left the line out
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins explaining רבה בר שילא's reasoning: since all the properties now belonged to רב חייא אריכא, it seemed not to matter which ones she collected from.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first he thought: these and those are both his. What difference does it make to me whether from these or from those?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts explaining the thinking behind רבה בר שילא's mistake. The next step shows why this thinking is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חייא אריכא inherited his brother's land, so both his own land and the inherited land belonged to him. רבה בר שילא assumed it made no difference which land the widow took, so he saw no need to state that the land came from the deceased.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, originally
His
What difference does it make to me?

phrases.english: At first he thought:
these and those are his,
phrases.notes: "These and those" are רב חייא אריכא's own land and the land he inherited from his brother.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי מֵהָנֵי, מָה לִי מֵהָנֵי,
phrases.english: what difference to me from these, what difference to me from those,

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא הוּא סְבַר הָנֵי וְהָנֵי דִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the claim in step 21 that רבה בר שילא erred, and sets up the continuation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה בר שילא originally thought it made no difference which of the heir's properties the widow collected from.

steps.title: Why it does matter which fields are written in the document
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רבה בר שילא's reasoning. If the document does not say which fields were the husband's, the widow may improve the wrong fields while her husband's fields lose value. Then the heir can say, 'Take yours, give me mine,' and people will speak badly about the court.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. Sometimes she goes and improves those fields, while her husband's fields lose value. Then he says to her: 'Take yours and give me mine.' And people will come to spread a bad name about the court.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the reasoning he just described in רבה בר שילא's name. He shows that it does matter which fields the document names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר שילא thought that once all the land belonged to one owner, naming the exact fields did not matter. רבא shows the danger: she works hard on fields that were never her husband's, the heir neglects her husband's fields, and later he swaps them back. So the document must say exactly which fields she may collect from, and leaving that out is a real flaw, not a small slip.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so. A phrase used to reject an idea that was just said.
She improves (the land)
They lose value (literally, 'they are put to shame')
A bad name, gossip, criticism
The court

steps.whatToRemember: An authorization to collect (אדרכתא) must name exactly which fields belonged to the late husband. Leaving that out is a real flaw, which is why רבה בר שילא's document gave the widow nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the widow's case. It explains why the flawed authorization gave her nothing, and why רבא would not treat the mistake as a טעות סופר.

phrases.english: But that is not so.
Sometimes she goes and improves them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the heir's own fields, which she thinks she will be collecting from.

phrases.english: and those of her husband lose value,
and he says to her:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the heir who now owns all the fields.

phrases.english: Take yours and give me mine,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָתֵי לְאַפּוֹקֵי לַעַז עַל בֵּי דִינָא.
phrases.english: and people come to spread a bad name about the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning given for רבה בר שילא in step 22, which completes רבא's answer from step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that it does not matter which fields the widow collects from once they all belong to one owner.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the risk that she improves the heir's fields while her husband's fields are neglected, and is later forced to swap. That would cause her a loss and bring criticism on the court.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הנושא
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula that ends the chapter called הנושא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter הנושא.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter is over, and this is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הנושא is the name of the chapter that just ended, taken from its opening word. Saying הדרן expresses the hope to come back and learn this chapter again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The line said at the end of a chapter.
The name of the chapter just finished (literally, 'one who marries')

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter הנושא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the widow's case is finished.

steps.title: Two judges of decrees in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה introduces two judges, אדמון and חנן בן אבישלום. It tells us חנן gives his own ruling on two matters and אדמון on seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two judges of decrees in ירושלים: אדמון and חנן בן אבישלום. חנן states two matters; אדמון states seven.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins. The משנה introduces two judges and tells us how many rulings each one is known for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opening line is a setup. It names the two judges and counts their rulings, and the cases themselves come next. The משנה is about to go through these matters one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Judges of decrees. Important judges in ירושלים who issued rulings.
One of the two judges
The other judge

phrases.english: Two judges of decrees

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, אַדְמוֹן וְחָנָן בֶּן אֲבִישָׁלוֹם.
phrases.english: there were in Jerusalem: Admon and Hanan ben Avishalom.
Hanan states two matters,
Admon states seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces אדמון and חנן בן אבישלום and the number of matters each one rules on.

steps.title: First case: a husband overseas and a wife asking for support
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets up the first of חנן's matters: a husband went overseas, and his wife asks for food money from his property. The text stops right as חנן is about to give his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who went overseas, and his wife is asking for food money. חנן says:
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out the first case so it can give the judges' rulings. This line is a setup, and חנן's actual ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is away, and the wife asks the court to support her from his property. The question is how the court handles this while he is not there, and חנן's answer follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Overseas, a faraway land
She demands, claims
Food and support

phrases.english: One who went overseas
and his wife is demanding support,
Hanan says:

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָלַךְ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם וְאִשְׁתּוֹ תּוֹבַעַת מְזוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins listing the matters announced in step 25, starting with חנן's first ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a wife asking for support while her husband is overseas. חנן's ruling follows.
